verdict.root_cause: Payment's OTLP traces exporter endpoint was rewritten five times by platform-automation and left pointing at loopback (http://127.0.0.1:4317) about 7 minutes before onset [tr_4ee3762a334c]. The last sampled payment span is at 19:21:18, seconds before that final application, and no trace exists at the 19:29:16 onset [tr_fb545a7a5108]; span-derived metrics for payment are empty throughout [tr_45a53db95206][tr_8a968aa941ab]. Payment itself is healthy: zero error-matching log lines over the window containing onset [tr_8d91e69b300f] and a successful card transaction logged two minutes after onset [tr_24b2e5ff92f3]. The wrong endpoint value is itself the failure — telemetry export is directed at an address nothing serves, producing a data-absence signal that read as a critical payment incident.
verdict.reasoning: Three channels agree payment is doing its work correctly: sub-1.5ms Charge spans with no error status and checkout flows completing past Charge [tr_fb545a7a5108], no error log lines across a window that fully covers 19:29:16 [tr_8d91e69b300f], and a successful transaction after onset [tr_24b2e5ff92f3]. What is missing is payment's telemetry, not payment's requests. The only change in the window is one variable, the traces exporter endpoint, last applied 7 minutes before onset and pointing at loopback [tr_4ee3762a334c] — and sampled spans stop six seconds before that application [tr_fb545a7a5108]. This is bad_config rather than a mere upstream act: the wrong address is the mechanism that breaks the export.
open_questions: Whether the 19:29:16 alert fired on a customer-facing symptom or on telemetry absence — the alert predicate is unknown.
Whether a collector actually listens on 127.0.0.1:4317 on payment's host; the endpoint is only wrong if nothing is there.
The 19:21–19:31 interval is largely unobserved (truncated logs, no sampled traces), and the other two blast-radius services were never dispatched against.

alternatives.root_cause: Payment's span-metrics and trace gap is a long-standing instrumentation/label mismatch unrelated to the config edits, and the real incident lies in an undispatched service such as checkout or frontend.
alternatives.why_not: Nothing was gathered on checkout or frontend, so this is unsupported speculation; the config edit's timing against the last sampled span is concrete.

alternatives.root_cause: A transient payment degradation occurred inside the unobserved 19:21–19:31 window and resolved before the last log line.
alternatives.why_not: The error-substring query covers that interval and returned nothing [tr_8d91e69b300f], and payment was completing transactions at window close [tr_24b2e5ff92f3].

proposal.expected_effect: Reverting payment's environment removes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4317 applied 7m before onset. Observable: a Tempo query for service=payment should again return PaymentService/Charge server spans plus the inner charge span under checkout's Charge, sub-1.5ms, as seen up to 19:21:18 and not after. I do not predict traces_span_metrics_calls_total for payment becomes non-empty — that series was already empty in the pre-change baseline and is not a valid confirmation signal.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if sampled checkout traces still show no payment child spans 10 minutes after the recreate, meaning loopback was not what severed export. Also materially wrong if the 19:29:16 alert keeps firing once payment traces return: the alert predicate is unknown, so this may fix only visibility while a real fault stays unlocated.
proposal.risk: The changes oscillate set/revert, so the recorded 'previous' value may itself be wrong, and automation may re-apply loopback within 10-15 minutes unless stopped. The action recreates the container of a service currently completing card transactions with zero error lines, so in-flight charges fail during the recreate — a self-inflicted outage if the diagnosis is wrong.
proposal.blast_radius: payment only, for the recreate duration. checkout sees Charge connection resets and frontend sees them via checkout. Trace export traffic moves from loopback back to the prior collector address.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A single critical alert on payment, a revenue-path service with downstream checkout and frontend exposure, cannot be dismissed without evidence. No open incidents to attribute it to and nothing in the alert pattern suggests a specific fault class.
